sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 21 (#20), Internal Quality Checks row 21 (no additional annotation); all Quality Checks and Deterministic Checks cell values read
evidence: Assigned row only. Workbook Quality Checks!A21:D21 and Internal Quality Checks row 21 require a static baseline and deterministic pinned values; quality-checks.md:86-88 specifies repeatable seeding and fixed-clock rules. Frozen solution/solve.sh:33 copies the shipped app; it does not generate or download its source. solution/app/src/db.js:14-15 reads the co-located static roster, and :123-179 seeds fixed IDs and values in a transaction only when users are absent. The two seed_data.json files are byte-identical (SHA256 1b39015461a7a4f23b835aeea9584caffd0266c64d394778376cbd6c8a18bcf7), with reference_moment 2026-08-01T00:00:00Z. src/rules.js:17-21 reads the stored clock; :24-47 uses UTC arithmetic over explicit dates; :142-150 computes referral vesting against its supplied stored-clock argument. src/index.js:49 defines now() as R.refAt(db), and financial mutations use it. No wall-clock read or off-origin data fetch was found in the solution; bootstrap.js proxies only loopback. src/index.js:50,99 and src/change-sets.js:87 generate new record/session identifiers, never seeded figures. Public hireops_rules.md section 5 expressly permits generated record IDs; section 11 prescribes no generated record format. Those IDs are not pinned values. Independently recomputed all 37 frozen task and 34 frozen rule hashes against manifest.json: no mismatch. Reviewed lifecycle driver and raw result; their indexed hashes match 05780ac5eb6f1e441ef5a946a36f466ad7cdee7ae239b5f7d7d9f5933f39e024 and 368261834b06931f2e8ac0fa0fd909a435e7ae28a6c30444c3ff48240d27bb24 respectively, and all result solution_app_sha256 entries match the frozen manifest. That finite Linux run observed fresh installation, retained saved data across process replacement, and reinstall restoring 7 requisitions/13 offers. It checks counts rather than exhaustive row equality; repeatability of pinned contents is additionally supported by the explicit static seed insertion code. No configured judge, Oracle/model score, or blanket runtime clearance is asserted.
counterexample: Adversarial source reasoning (not a new provider or mutation run): a baseline that seeded a random reference moment, fetched live rates, or reset persistent rows at boot could drift graded figures; the local roster, fixed-clock functions, and users-count seeding guard exclude those mechanisms here. A conforming app that generates new opaque IDs or omits optional operational demonstration history must not fail merely for differing IDs or seed counts; public sections 1/5/11 permit those alternatives, and this finding imposes no such requirement.
